note: Every threshold has a why. A value that proves infeasible or wrong changes here, with a written reason, in the same commit that needs the change.

text.why: WCAG 2.x success criterion 1.4.3, level AA, for text below 18 pt (14 pt bold).

component.why: WCAG 2.x 1.4.11 for interface components and graphical objects.

aaaText.why: WCAG 2.x 1.4.6, level AAA. Reported for every text pair and never a gate.

minDistance.why: Smallest pairwise OKLab distance that keeps two roles of a distinct set apart under normal vision. It is the brief's value; Okabe-Ito's own minimum is 0.156 under normal vision.

cvd.method: Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) matrices at severity 1.0, applied in linear light, for protan, deutan and tritan. One method for every family.

severity.why: Complete dichromacy is the hardest case a gate can name; partial severities pass when this passes.

minDistance.why: The same OKLab distance as under normal vision, so a declared reinforced pair is the only way out.

darkRoom.why: Ambient light added to both luminances for a projector in a dark room (the brief's value).

litRoom.why: The same for a projector in a lit room.

office-screen.why: A reader at a desk on an ordinary monitor. The gate is the declared pairs at WCAG AA; AAA and APCA are reported.

apca.why: APCA Lc is reported for web-UI profiles only (office-screen, editor, night). The apca-w3 licence excludes clinical, human-safety and non-web use.

editor.why: Code on the editor background, the current line and the selection, as the shipped themes draw them.

textOnBackground.why: Every syntax role is body text on the editor background: WCAG AA.

textOnCurrentLine.why: The caret sits on the current line most of the time, so syntax roles must clear AA there too.

textOnSelection.why: Selected text is transient and editors draw the selection translucent; the brief sets 3:1.

cvd.why: Colour vision deficiency. A distinct set keeps its pairs apart under each simulation, except declared reinforced pairs.

night.why: Reading, writing and code in a dark room. The argument is glare, halation and dark adaptation, not sleep.

darkBackgroundLuminance.why: Relative luminance of the dark ground: between sRGB greys of about 13 and 29, off black without turning grey.

darkBackgroundTarget.why: Decision D11: the upper half of the band, keeping the sea hue. Reported as a warning when missed.

bodyContrast.why: Body text at 7:1 to 11:1. With the brightness cap below, the upper bound is out of reach and the usable range is 7:1 to about 8.6:1.

maxTokenLuminance.why: No token brighter than a relative luminance of 0.45, so nothing blooms in a dark-adapted eye.

textHue.why: No text role in the blue to violet hue range at visible chroma: short wavelengths scatter more and blur text in the dark.

lamplightPaperLuminance.why: The light mode is dimmed paper for night reading, about half the luminance of a daytime paper.

lamplightBodyContrast.why: Body text on the dimmed paper.

forced-colors.why: Windows High Contrast and other forced-colours modes replace every colour. Focus, selection and state markers must survive. Checked by DOM assertions on a Playwright render with forcedColors active; screenshots are kept as artefacts.

markers.why: The four states the family relies on. Each needs a marker that is not colour alone (outline, border, underline or weight).

projector.why: Slides in a room with ambient light. Flare is added to both luminances.

flagFields.why: Flag fields stay apart after flare (brief).

sunlight.why: A phone or tablet in daylight.

meaningfulPairs.why: My addition: a distinct set that opts in to sunlight stays as far apart after glare as the normal-vision gate requires. The brief gives no set gate for this profile.

aged-eye.why: A reader whose lens has yellowed. An approximation: Machado tritanomaly at severity 0.5, then flare 0.02. The spectral route is the Pokorny, Smith and Lutze (1987) lens density model.

meaningfulPairs.why: Pairs that carry meaning stay apart after the simulation (brief).

print-grey.why: Greyscale laser print. CIE L* from luminance.

distinctLstar.why: Members of a distinct set differ by at least 12 L*, unless they carry a pattern or line style (brief).

eink.why: E-ink readers and tablets: sixteen grey levels.

levelGap.why: Distinct roles land at least two levels apart (brief).

photocopy.why: A photocopy clips highlights and shadows.

fills.why: Meaningful fills sit between L* 25 and 80 or carry a pattern (brief).

overlay.why: Annotation fills composited at their declared opacity over every family's ground.

textOnFillLight.why: Text on a fill over a light ground (brief).

textOnFillDark.why: Text on a fill over a dark ground (brief).

fillFromGround.why: A fill is visible against the ground (brief).

fillsApart.why: Fills differ from one another, normal and CVD (brief).

severityStepLstar.why: Adjacent severity levels differ by 8 L* (brief).

severityStepDistance.why: And by 0.06 under each CVD simulation (brief).

criticalRedExclusion.why: No non-status role within 0.10 of the critical red (brief).

figure.why: Charts. The categorical scale must match or beat Okabe-Ito's minimum pairwise OKLab distance under normal vision and each CVD simulation, and beat it on one of three further measures. See the Enderby section of the brief. The reference palettes are in tests/fixtures/reference/palettes.json.

categoricalCount.why: An ordered categorical set of eight, most separable first (brief).

markContrast.why: WCAG 1.4.11 for graphical objects: a mark keeps 3:1 against the figure background, or has an outline token that does (brief).

sequentialUniformity.why: My starting value: the largest step of a sequential ramp is at most 1.35 times the smallest, in OKLab. Viridis and cividis sampled at 5 to 11 steps reach 1.14 to 1.27, so both pass.

divergingSymmetry.why: My starting value: matched steps on either side of the centre differ by at most 0.03 of OKLab lightness, about three L* points, so neither side reads as the stronger one (brief: symmetric lightness at matched steps).

divergingCentreChroma.why: My starting value: the centre of a diverging ramp is a neutral, so its OKLCH chroma is at most 0.02 (brief: neutral light centre).

divergingAxis.why: My starting value: the two sides of a diverging ramp stay 0.08 apart in OKLab under each CVD simulation, in the outer half of the ramp, where the two meanings are strongest (brief: CVD-safe axis). Okabe-Ito's own smallest distance under deutan is 0.075.

focusContext.why: My starting value: the one strong colour of a focus-and-context chart is at least 0.12 from the context grey, so the focus cannot be mistaken for context (brief: a focus-and-context pattern).

contextChroma.why: My starting value: the context colour is a grey, so its OKLCH chroma is at most 0.02 (brief: one strong colour plus greys).
